note: Small Mark Twain National Forest campground in a CCC-planted shortleaf pine stand on Route Y west of New Bloomfield, with a day-use field and a Cedar Creek Trail trailhead. Asphalt spurs; two sites take RVs up to 34 ft and the other six are shorter, with no per-site lengths published. Eight people per site. --Claude
summary: Confirmed on the Forest Service page: Site Open, 8 single sites, $15, no hookups, potable water, vault toilet, season April 15-December 1 (2026). Two sites take up to 34 ft; lengths of the other six are not published. Not on recreation.gov. Pin is on a private driveway across the highway - move 75 m.
flags: RIG LENGTH: the page's site-specific wording is 'Two sites can accommodate up to 34’ RVs. Six sites can accommodate RVs less than 34’', with 'Vehicle Clearance: No restrictions' and 'Pavement Type of Parking: Asphalt'. No per-site lengths are published anywhere I found (not on recreation.gov, so no catalog), and the spurs are under pine canopy on imagery, so I could not measure them. Plainly: two sites certainly take a 23-ft rig; for the other six the page only says 'less than 34 ft', which does not exclude 23 ft but does not confirm it. Kept (two sure RV sites; unclear pad size is a caveat, not a drop).

PIN MOVE (75 m): stored 38.7578,-92.1423 lands on a private house's driveway on the south side of Route Y. The campground entrance is on the north side; the Forest Service's own point 38.758438,-92.142538 sits on the entrance drive beside the day-use field. Suggest 38.75844,-92.14254. The camp spurs themselves are hidden under the pines west of the drive, so this is the entrance drive, not a pad.
SEASON: stored approximate Apr 1-Dec 31 (derived) replaced by the page's 'Open April 15 - December 1, 2026'.
STATUS/ALERTS: page banner 'Site Open'; the only alert shown is a forest-wide list item for the Chadwick motorized trail (another district). No alert for this site.
PHONE: none stored. The page gives the Houston/Rolla/Cedar Creek Ranger District, 417-967-4194.
Not waterfront confirmed (no water body; pine upland).
